newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares rally for second day, SBI up six pct.
newsitem.headline: India shares rally for second day, SBI up six pct.

text.p: Share prices at Indian bourses rose for the second straight day on Tuesday with spotlight on State Bank of India (SBI) shares amid market talk of raising a foreign investment limit, dealers said.

"The market showed a kind of weakness early on..but spurted in the latter half of trading..," said dealer Vetri Subramaniam at institutional brokerage SSKI Securities. "It was a traders' market..." he said.
SBI shot up 18.0 rupees, or 6.11 percent, to close at 312.50 in hectic volumes of over 11 million shares, thus making it one of the best performing bellwether stocks on Tuesday.
Market talk of a relaxation in the 20 percent foreign buying limit to 24 percent in SBI spurred the price rise, dealers said.

"This will help a great deal to stoke up buying appetite of foreign institutional investors," said senior trader Ramnik Parekh. He said continued speculative buying ahead of government announcements was likely to sustain the market's upward trend.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Monday said new economic policy measures would be announced in the next few days.
Gowda said the government would announce the policy measures this week before he and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram leave to attend the World Economic Forum in Davos on January 31.
Tuesday's BSE index rise came on the back of nearly a four percent surge on Monday.

"The prime minister's statement came as a shot in the arm for speculators who indulged in frenzied buying, forcing bears to stay on the sidelines," said Suresh Aggarwal of Delhi brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Dealers however said hesitation by operators to take delivery of stocks on the last day of settlement at the National Stock Exchange helped pivotals end lower than BSE rates.
TISCO rose 3.0 rupees to 211.0 and Reliance 8.0 to 280.50.
